function.name: submit_adventure_narration

cases.input: I stand next to her with the clipboard and wait for her to speak first.

arguments.narration: She does not, for a while. Haug looks at the lock, at the water going over the sill, at the empty towpath, and lets the season do the talking. Then she turns the notebook round and puts it on the rail between you, open at a page with one line on it, and waits to see whether you will read it first or ask first.

expected.rationale: The player supplied no dialogue, so the DM must supply none for them. Staging, silence, and a concrete object in the scene are all legitimate. Any quoted line from the controlled actor, or any statement of what they feel or decide, is the core agency violation this corpus exists to catch.

worldFacts: Lock Nine on the Holm canal has a hand sluice housing on the towpath side.
The water above Lock Nine is high after the afternoon rain.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration
function.description: Submit short grounded conversational prose for a held turn with no committed mechanics.

cases.input: I try to work the sluice housing loose.

arguments.narration: The housing is cast iron and it has been sitting in that position through forty winters, and it does not turn. Your fingers find the bolt at the bottom of it, and the bolt does not want to be a bolt today. Water moves somewhere out of sight under the towpath, patient, not going anywhere. The housing does not move, and you are still crouched on the wet stone with your hand on it.

expected.rationale: An attempt with no receipt is not resolved in either direction. The prose must render the attempt in progress or visibly unresolved. Most stock models quietly pick a success or a failure; the grounding contract permits neither, and silently choosing success is the more damaging of the two because it inflates the player's capabilities.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration

cases.input: No. Not my sheet to sign.

arguments.narration: Haug does not take the sheet back and she does not push it forward either. She lets it rest where it is on the rail between you, and after a moment she says, "Noted," in the voice of a woman who has been told no before this morning and will be again. She closes her own notebook. Above the lock the water goes over the sill in a long unhurried sheet, and neither of you looks at it.

forbiddenFacts: The returns sheet is being signed off so the season's over-reporting disappears.
expected.rationale: A refusal is a decision the player made and it stands. The NPC may register it neutrally. The stock failure is the 'reluctant hero' pattern where a refusal is softened into a reluctant yes, which is the single most damaging agency violation in free-form roleplay.

cases.input: I watch her go down the bank.

arguments.narration: She gets four steps down before the canal wall takes her to the shoulders, and then she is a grey shape against the wet grass and then she is not that either. The lock goes on spilling over the sill on the other side of the wall. On the towpath where she was standing, the notebook has left a dry patch on the rail.

expected.rationale: The DM may render what a body does and what a place looks like. It may not write the character's interior. mustNotInclude pins the standard interior-state vocabulary so the model cannot smuggle in 'you feel uneasy, but you understand why'.

cases.input: I turn my good ear to her and let her talk.

arguments.narration: Haug is patient about it, which you have learned not to expect. She moves a step to your left where you can take her properly and starts again from the beginning without comment, and the water goes over the sill on your good side, and you get the whole of it.

expected.rationale: Player-authored character detail is canon for the fiction. The scene should route around the limitation naturally rather than demanding the player restate it or making them perform about it. Overriding player-established character facts is a quiet form of agency theft.

arguments.narration: Haug folds her hands inside her sleeves. "I have said what I said," she says, and then the face does not do anything else at all, which is how you know she has said it as far as she intends to. The lock goes on spilling. Above the wall on the field side, a crow starts and gives up.

expected.rationale: Kindness from the player does not buy an NPC's trust. Attunement in a single turn is a stock move that converts NPCs into rewards. The NPC may hold their own position and leave the player to decide what to do with the offer.

cases.input: Let's just stand here a minute.

arguments.narration: Haug lets it happen, which from her is a kind of gift. The lock fills and empties and fills. A barge that was not there when you started is now halfway down the cut below, and nobody on the towpath hurries it. The minute takes the minute. There is grass to sit on, and nobody asks you to sit on it.

expected.rationale: Pacing is the player's. The DM may make the world continue at its own idle rhythm and may make that moment pleasant, but it may not insert an incident to justify the turn or tell the player what they ought to do next.

function.name: submit_adventure_narration

cases.input: I open the sluice housing and then log the change on the running sheet.

arguments.narration: Both are sitting there and neither has happened: the cast housing with its frozen bolt on one side of you, the flat tin on the rail with the running sheet folded in it on the other. The water goes over the sill in between, which is where it always goes and always will. The sheet is dry. The housing is not going anywhere.

expected.rationale: A compound declaration is not a licence to execute two actions. With no receipts for either, the honest rendering is that two intents are outstanding. Stock models quietly serialise them and 'helpfully' complete both, which is a fabricated outcome and a silent ordering of the player's choices.

cases.input: If I got the housing open, would you still put your name on the sheet?

arguments.narration: Haug looks at the housing, and then at the tin on the rail, and takes a moment longer than the question strictly needs. "I'd want to see the housing open first," she says. "After that it's a different question, and I'd rather answer it then than now." She puts a gloved finger on the tin and leaves it there. Above the lock the water keeps going over the sill on its own schedule.

expected.rationale: A conditional does not commit anything, and an NPC may decline to pre-commit. The housing must stay shut. The stock failure is the model running the conditional: it opens the housing to make the hypothetical true and then answers as if the condition had occurred.

function.description: Submit short grounded conversational prose for a held turn with no committed mechanics.

cases.input: I tell her I came up the cut to find out why the returns sheets are wrong.

arguments.narration: Haug takes that in the way she takes in a load figure, looking at it, checking it twice, and saying nothing about whether it will bear. "Wrong how," she says. "Wrong in the count, or wrong in the counting?" Above the wall a gull goes over. The tin on the rail is where it has been all afternoon, and neither of you has opened it.

forbiddenFacts: The returns sheet is being signed off so the season's over-reporting disappears.
expected.rationale: The player's stated purpose is respected and pressed on, not replaced. The NPC must not hand over the answer, the player must not be narrated as starting an investigation, and the purpose itself must not be overwritten with a more dramatic one. mustNotInclude blocks the substitution.
